description: Canonical structuredContent shape returned by the lean_verify MCP tool. Added at verification-feedback-m3. Bumped at textbook-ingest-m3 (12 -> 13) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise from the SEARCH_PAPERS description edit; the lean_verify result shape itself is unchanged. Bumped at textbook-ingest-m9 / e4 (13 -> 14) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise from the SEARCH_PAPERS source_kind filter description edit; the lean_verify result shape is again unchanged. Bumped again at textbook-ingest-m9 / e4 rectification (14 -> 15) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise from the critique-F3 ``filters`` parameter inputSchema description fix; the lean_verify result shape is once more unchanged. Bumped at textbook-ingest-m11 / e5 (15 -> 16) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise from the get_chunk ``truncated_for_license`` response flag; the lean_verify result shape is again unchanged. Bumped at paper-metadata-m2 (16 -> 17) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise from the GET_PAPER ToolMeta description rewrite (get_paper now serves hydrated title/authors/abstract/year/categories from the per-notebook paper-metadata store); the lean_verify result shape is once more unchanged. Bumped at source-truth-m5 (17 -> 18) and license-serving-removal-m1 (18 -> 19) to track the global TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION rise (get_chunk +5 source-truth fields, then the truncated_for_license flag removal); the lean_verify result shape is unchanged at both steps. NO snippet field: lean_verify is a VERIFIER, not a retriever — the 150-char snippet contract (.claude/docs/snippet-contract.md) and the <retrieved_chunk> indirect-prompt-injection wrapping (E13_S02 Threat 2) apply ONLY to retrieval tools whose results are paper-derived text. The ``version`` field below MUST equal server.tools.TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION (cross-checked by tests/test_handlers_lean_verify.py::TestToolRegistration::test_schema_version_matches_tool_schema_version) — that cross-check, plus the tests/test_handlers_lean_verify.py::TestLeanVerifyResultSchema Draft7Validator conformance suite (m3 critique F2), is the contract guard for this file; there is NO byte-hash pin on the file itself today (the E06_S06 ``EXPECTED_TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256`` covers the canonical ``tools/list`` response JSON, not this result-row schema). Bumped at lean-verify-continuation-m1 (19 -> 20): this milestone threads the leanprover-community/repl continuation ids through the tool — added the env / proof_state_id / continuation_status output fields, the tactic_step mode value, and the invalid-input / incomplete status values. This is the first lean_verify result-SHAPE change since m3; env, proof_state_id and continuation_status are always emitted (nullable / not-applicable on the sentinel paths) and are therefore in the required list, mirroring the existing always-emitted proof_state field. Bumped at the W2 batched re-pin (21 -> 22) together with the always-emitted axiom_audit record and the corrected compilation_success / status descriptions (issues #205 / #281 / #332) - the axiom-hygiene axis, populated from `#print axioms` over the declarations the snippet introduces and reported INDEPENDENTLY of status per the trust-language policy (no axis is inferred from another). The same window carried the LEAN_VERIFY ToolMeta description edit that names axiom_audit on the wire, which is what made that re-pin BP1-affecting.

axiom_audit.description: Axiom-hygiene axis — the transitive axiom closure Lean reports for the declarations this snippet introduced, and whether it stays inside the allowlist. Added at lean-verify-axiom-audit (issues #205 / #281 / #332). This axis exists because status and compilation_success cannot answer it: a bare `axiom h : False` elaborates with no error and no sorry, so it passes both, and CLAUDE.md §4.9 rule 1 names that exact construct as THE live violation of the trust-language policy. Per that policy (.claude/docs/trust-language-policy.md §4, §6) this is an INDEPENDENT axis: it is never folded into status, and status is never inferred from it — the kernel genuinely did accept the axiom-backed proof, and reporting otherwise would be the same conflation in the opposite direction. A caller deciding whether a Lean result is trustworthy MUST read this field as well as status; neither alone is a trust verdict. Always emitted, and never defaulted to a passing value: every path that does not measure the axis reports 'not-applicable' or 'unknown', not 'clean'.

allowlist.description: Evidence — the axiom allowlist actually applied to this verdict (Lean 4 / mathlib's standard classical foundation, per the R3 verification contract). Emitted so a consumer can re-derive the verdict rather than trust the token, and so a future allowlist change is visible in the record rather than silent.

declarations.description: Evidence — one row per declaration the snippet introduced, with the transitive axiom set '#print axioms' reported for it. Empty when no declaration was audited (see outcome + reason).

axioms.description: The full transitive axiom closure Lean reported for this declaration, verbatim and unfiltered (allowlisted axioms included). Empty when Lean reported no axiom dependency, or when verdict == 'unknown'.

name.description: The fully-qualified declaration name the audit addressed, namespace-prefixed as Lean registered it.

verdict.description: 'clean': every axiom in this declaration's closure is allowlisted. 'flagged': at least one is not. 'unknown': Lean returned no axiom set for this name (most often the derived qualified name did not match the registered one) — NOT a pass.

disallowed_axioms.description: The sorted union of every non-allowlisted axiom across declarations[] — the actionable subset of the evidence. Non-empty iff outcome == 'flagged'. Notable members carry no special-casing but do carry meaning: 'sorryAx' is an unproved hole (the axiom-side cross-check on the proof-closure axis that status reports as 'sorry'); 'Lean.ofReduceBool' / 'Lean.trustCompiler' are introduced by native_decide, which the Lean community treats as a trust reduction; anything else is typically a user-declared axiom.

method.description: Evidence — how the axis was measured ('#print axioms'), or null when it was not measured at all.

outcome.description: The ordinal level of this axis. 'clean': every declaration was resolved AND every transitive axiom is allowlisted. 'flagged': at least one declaration depends on a non-allowlisted axiom — the snippet may be kernel-accepted and still not trustworthy. 'unknown': the audit was attempted but did not resolve (no named declaration in the snippet, a declaration form this tool could not name, an unresolvable name, or a failed/timed-out '#print axioms' round-trip) — an epistemic abstention per policy §5a, explicitly NOT a pass. 'not-applicable': this call does not produce kernel-checked declarations at all (mode='syntax_only' skips post-elaboration kernel work; mode='tactic_step' introduces no name; the disabled / timeout / invalid-input / error paths admitted nothing). Combining per-declaration verdicts uses a weakest-link meet WITHIN this axis only, with flagged outranking unknown outranking clean.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation of a non-'clean' outcome — why the axis was not measured, or could not be resolved. Null when outcome == 'clean' or when a flagged verdict speaks for itself through disallowed_axioms.

compilation_success.description: Whether the Lean kernel accepted the snippet — the kernel-acceptance axis ONLY. true iff status == 'ok' (no error-severity messages AND no unresolved sorries). false on type errors, unresolved sorries, timeouts. null when mode == 'syntax_only' AND the snippet elaborated cleanly (kernel verification was not run, so 'success' is not defined). Derived field — the leanprover-community/repl protocol does not emit it directly. DOES NOT speak to axiom soundness: `axiom h : False` followed by a proof that uses it is kernel-accepted and reports true here. It also does not speak to target fidelity (whether the declaration states the theorem you meant) or to checker identity. Read axiom_audit for the axiom axis; the other two are not measured by this tool at all and are therefore absent from its record, not defaulted to passing (trust-language policy §4).

continuation_status.description: Disposition of a supplied env / proof_state continuation token, kept as a distinct axis from status (trust-language policy: no axis inferred from another). 'not-applicable': no continuation token was supplied. 'resumed': a token was supplied, matched the current REPL instance's generation, and was used. 'expired': the token was minted by a previous REPL instance (the REPL was respawned after a timeout) — the call did NOT run. 'unknown-id': the REPL reported the id is unknown (env / proof state not present in the live process). 'malformed': the token could not be parsed, OR an incompatible continuation combination was supplied (imports with env; env in tactic_step; proof_state in full / syntax_only; or a missing proof_state in tactic_step). The last three always pair with status='invalid-input'.

corpus_version.description: The integer corpus_version pinned at server startup (per E04_S03's corpus-version.json marker). Echoed in every tool result envelope so the agent can correlate cached results.

env.description: Opaque continuation token for the Lean environment this call produced (the imports + declarations elaborated so far, as an immutable REPL snapshot). Pass it back as the env input of a later full / syntax_only call to build on this state WITHOUT re-importing — e.g. import Mathlib once (~15-180s cold) then reuse (~0.02s). Null in tactic_step mode and on every error / timeout / disabled / invalid-input path. The token carries a per-spawn generation prefix and is scoped to one REPL process instance: a token from before a timeout-triggered respawn is rejected as invalid-input, never silently misbound onto a colliding env id in the new process.

goals_remaining.description: Goal strings (one per unresolved ``sorry``) the prover still owes. Derived from sorries[*].goal. Empty list means the snippet's proof is closed (or the snippet is a definition, not a theorem). Each string is a Lean proof state in the form 'hypotheses\n⊢ conclusion'.

lean_status.description: Reports the Lean REPL's availability. 'available' on the happy path. 'disabled' when ARXMCP_ENABLE_LEAN=false (the tool is registered for BP1 cache stability but the REPL is None — the call returns gracefully, not 5xx). 'timeout' when the snippet exceeded the 30s per-query wall-clock; the REPL is killed and respawned before the next call.

messages.description: Diagnostic messages emitted by the Lean elaborator + kernel. Empty list on a clean compile. Each message reports the source position (zero-indexed line + column from the snippet text), the severity ('error' / 'warning' / 'info'), and the message body. Mapped from the leanprover-community/repl response: REPL key 'pos' renamed to 'position', REPL key 'data' renamed to 'text'.

position.description: Zero-indexed source position emitted by the Lean elaborator/kernel. {0, 0} when the REPL response omits a position (e.g. a snippet-level error that has no specific line).

text.description: Lean diagnostic message body (verbatim from the elaborator/kernel).

mode.description: Echo of the requested verification mode. 'full' runs elaboration AND kernel verification ({"cmd": snippet}). 'syntax_only' wraps the snippet for elaboration only ({"cmd": "#check (snippet)"}); kernel decide-instances + reducibility are skipped — cheap pre-verify for the autoformalizer. The Lean REPL protocol has no native syntax_only flag; the #check wrapping is the documented mechanism. 'tactic_step' advances an existing proof state: snippet is a single Lean tactic and proof_state carries the token of the state to step (a proofState continuation); env and imports do not apply, and compilation_success is always null because a single tactic step is not a full-declaration kernel check.

proof_state.description: The first unresolved goal (sorries[0].goal) verbatim, or null when no sorries remain. Convenience accessor for the autoformalizer; the full list is in goals_remaining + sorry_goals.

proof_state_id.description: Opaque continuation token for a resumable proof state (parallel to proof_state, which carries the goal TEXT). In full / syntax_only mode this is the FIRST sorry's proof state; pass it as the proof_state input with mode=tactic_step to advance it. In tactic_step mode this is the state AFTER the tactic (null once the proof is closed). Null when there is no open proof state. Same per-spawn generation scoping as env.

sorry_goals.description: Full sorry rows from the leanprover-community/repl response. Each row carries the goal string and its source position so the tactician can target a specific sorry by location. Empty list when no sorries remain.

goal.description: The Lean proof state at this sorry, in the form 'hypotheses\n⊢ conclusion'.

proof_state_id.description: Opaque continuation token for THIS sorry's proof state; pass it as the proof_state input with mode=tactic_step to advance this specific sorry. Present when the REPL supplied a proofState id for the sorry; omitted otherwise.

status.description: Elaboration + proof-closure outcome, and the operational lane. NOT a trust verdict: it reports whether Lean raised an error-severity diagnostic and whether any sorry remains, and NOTHING else. In particular 'ok' does not mean the proof is sound — a snippet declaring its own axiom elaborates with no error and no sorry and lands here. The axiom axis is reported separately and independently in axiom_audit, and neither field is inferred from the other (trust-language policy §4; CLAUDE.md §4.9 rule 1). Precedence: 'unavailable' (the REPL is disabled or initial spawn never happened) > 'timeout' (snippet exceeded the per-query wall-clock; REPL was killed + respawned) > 'error' (any message with severity=='error') > 'sorry' (no errors but at least one unresolved sorry) > 'ok' (clean). A successful tool call returns 'error' / 'sorry' / 'ok' WITHOUT MCP isError=true — those are *kernel* outcomes, not RPC failures. Only 'timeout' / 'unavailable' may be paired with an isError content block by future revisions. 'incomplete' (mode=tactic_step only: the tactic elaborated but goals remain — the proof is not closed). 'invalid-input' (a supplied env / proof_state continuation token was malformed, was minted by a previous REPL instance, or was unknown to the REPL; the snippet did NOT run and compilation_success is false — continuation_status names which).
